entries.sanskrit: दशमे काल-संप्रश्न- प्राप्तिं वक्तुं तद् उद्भवः । प्राकृतादि-विभागेन सर्गस् तु दशधोच्यते ॥१॥
word_for_word: the obtaining of the question about time in the tenth chapter
creation is said to be tenfold
through divisions beginning with the material
entries.literal_english: The tenth chapter explains the answer concerning time and the arising of Brahmā. Creation is described as tenfold through the divisions beginning with the material and continuing with the derivative creations.

entries.sanskrit: मे मया । वदस्व वद । भासयस्वेति वा ॥२॥
entries.literal_english: “Me” means “by me.” “Speak” means “tell us”; or it means “make the meaning shine forth.”

entries.sanskrit: सञ्चोदितः प्रार्थितः । हृदि-स्थान् एवाह, न तु ते प्रश्नास् तेन विस्मृता इत्य् अर्थः ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: “Prompted” means requested. He speaks of the questions as residing in his heart; the meaning is that he had not forgotten them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: sañcoditaḥ prārthitaḥ | hṛdi-sthān evāha, na tu te praśnās tena vismṛtā ity arthaḥ ||3||

entries.sanskrit: आत्मनि श्री-नारायणे आत्मानं मन आवेश्य ॥४॥
word_for_word: placing the mind in the Self
entries.literal_english: He placed his mind in the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: ātmani śrī-nārāyaṇe ātmānaṃ mana āveśya ||4||

entries.sanskrit: अब्ज-संभूतो ब्रह्मा यद् अधिष्ठाय स्थितः, कर्तरि क्तः । तत् पद्मम् अम्भश् च विलोक्य । कथं-भूतं पद्मम् अम्भश् च ? तेन प्रलय-कालेन कृतं वीर्यं यस्य तेन वायुना कम्पितं, न्यपाद् इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥५॥ विवृद्धं विज्ञानं बलं च यस्य । न्यपात् सर्वं पीतवान् ॥६॥
word_for_word: seeing the lotus and the waters
knowledge and power that had increased
entries.literal_english: Brahmā, born from the lotus on which he was established, saw the lotus and the waters. The lotus was shaken by the wind produced at the time of dissolution; Brahmā drank or absorbed the waters and saw the power and knowledge associated with creation. The commentary connects the two verses with his arising and his inspection of the lotus and cosmic waters.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.

entries.sanskrit: पुष्करं पद्मम् । प्राग्-लीनान् त्रील् लोकान् कल्पितास्मि स्रक्ष्यामि ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: “Lotus” means the lotus. I shall create the three worlds that had previously merged into the causal condition.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: puṣkaraṃ padmam | prāg-līnān trīl lokān kalpitāsmi srakṣyāmi ||7||

entries.sanskrit: भगवता स्वयं करणीये कर्मणि चोदितो नियुक्तः संस् तदा पद्म-कोशं प्रविश्य तम् एकम् एव त्रिधा लोक-रूपेण व्यभाङ्क्षीद् विबभाज । एकेन कमल-मुकुलेन कथं लोक-त्रय-सृष्टिर् इत्य् असंभावनां वारयितुं तस्य विशालताम् आह---द्वि-सप्तधा चतुर्दश-लोक-रूपेण । उरुधा ततोऽपि बहु-प्रकारेण । भाव्यं भावयितुं योग्यम् । अतो न तेन त्रि-लोकी-करणं चित्रम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥८॥
word_for_word: he divided the one into three
fit to be brought into being
entries.literal_english: Appointed by Bhagavān to perform the work that Bhagavān Himself would accomplish, Brahmā entered the lotus-bud and divided the one into the form of the worlds. To remove the doubt that one lotus-bud could produce three worlds, the commentary explains its vastness as fourteen worlds and as many divisions.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: bhagavatā svayaṃ karaṇīye karmaṇi codito niyuktaḥ saṃs tadā padma-kośaṃ praviśya tam ekam eva tridhā loka-rūpeṇa vyabhāṅkṣīd vibabhāja | ekena kamala-mukulena kathaṃ loka-traya-sṛṣṭir ity asaṃbhāvanāṃ vārayituṃ tasya viśālatām āha---dvi-saptadhā caturdaśa-loka-rūpeṇa | urudhā tato’pi bahu-prakāreṇa | bhāvyaṃ bhāvayituṃ yogyam | ato na tena tri-lokī-karaṇaṃ citram ity arthaḥ ||8||

entries.sanskrit: त्रि-लोकी-रूपेणैव विभागे हेतुम् आह---एतावांस् त्रि-लोकी-रूपो जीव-लोकस्य जीवानां भोग-स्थानस्य प्रत्य् अहं सृज्यस्य संस्था-भेदो रचनाविशेष उक्तः । ननु परमेष्ठिनोऽपि जीवत्वाविशेषाद् ब्रह्म-लोकस्यापि किम् इति प्रत्य् अहं सृष्टिर् न भवति तत्राह---हि यस्माद् निमित्तस्य निष्कामस्य धर्मस्य विपाकः फल-रूपोऽसौ । उपलक्षणम् एतत् सत्य-लोकस्य महः प्रभृति-लोकानां तद् वासिनां च । त्रै-लोक्यस्य काम्य-कर्म-फलत्वात् प्रतिकल्पम् उत्पत्ति-विनाशौ भवतः । महः प्रभृतीनाम् उपासनासमुचित-निष्काम-धर्म-फलत्वाद् द्वि-परार्ध-पर्यन्तं न नाशः । तत्र-स्थानां च ततः परं प्रायेण मुक्तिर् इति भावः ॥९॥
word_for_word: the reason for the threefold division
of the world of living beings
because it is the fruit of desired action
creation and destruction in every kalpa
because it is the fruit of desireless dharma
entries.literal_english: He explains the reason for the threefold division. This much is the three-world form, the particular arrangement of the places where living beings enjoy and the daily creation of embodied beings. Although Brahmā is also a jīva, his world is distinguished by his role as the supreme creator within the created order.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tri-lokī-rūpeṇaiva vibhāge hetum āha---etāvāṃs tri-lokī-rūpo jīva-lokasya jīvānāṃ bhoga-sthānasya praty ahaṃ sṛjyasya saṃsthā-bhedo racanāviśeṣa uktaḥ | nanu parameṣṭhino’pi jīvatvāviśeṣād brahma-lokasyāpi kim iti praty ahaṃ sṛṣṭir na bhavati tatrāha---hi yasmād nimittasya niṣkāmasya dharmasya vipākaḥ phala-rūpo’sau | upalakṣaṇam etat satya-lokasya mahaḥ prabhṛti-lokānāṃ tad vāsināṃ ca | trai-lokyasya kāmya-karma-phalatvāt pratikalpam utpatti-vināśau bhavataḥ | mahaḥ prabhṛtīnām upāsanāsamucita-niṣkāma-dharma-phalatvād dvi-parārdha-paryantaṃ na nāśaḥ | tatra-sthānāṃ ca tataḥ paraṃ prāyeṇa muktir iti bhāvaḥ ||9||

entries.sanskrit: काल-भेदेन लोक-सृष्टि-भेदं श्रुत्वा तम् एव कालं जिज्ञासुः पृच्छति । यत् कालाख्यं लक्षणं स्वरूपम् आत्थ अब्रवीः । कथं कालः कल्पते ? किं वा तस्य सूक्ष्मं स्थूलं च रूपं ? इति यथावद् वर्णयेत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥
entries.literal_english: After hearing that the creation of the worlds varies according to time, Vidura asks to know that very time: what is its defining nature, how does time operate, and what are its subtle and gross forms? He asks for a complete explanation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: kāla-bhedena loka-sṛṣṭi-bhedaṃ śrutvā tam eva kālaṃ jijñāsuḥ pṛcchati | yat kālākhyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ svarūpam āttha abravīḥ | kathaṃ kālaḥ kalpate ? kiṃ vā tasya sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ ca rūpaṃ ? iti yathāvad varṇayety arthaḥ ||10||

entries.sanskrit: तत्र सामान्यतः कालस्य स्वरूपम् अत्रोच्यते, उत्तराध्याये तु विशेषतः । गुणानां व्यतिकरो महद्-आदि-परिणामस् तेनैवाक्रियते यः, स काल इति शेषः । वक्ष्यते चैकादशे---गुण-व्यतिकरः कालः स्वभावः सूत्रम् एव च \[भा।पु। ११.२२.१३\] इति । स्वतस् तु निर्विशेषः । अप्रतिष्ठितः क्वाप्य् अपर्यवसितः, आद्य्-अन्त-शून्य इत्य् अर्थः । एतद् एव दर्शयितुम् ईश्वरः सृष्ट्य्-आदि तेन निमित्त-भूतेन करोतीत्य् आह---पुरुष इति । उपादीयते निमित्ततया स्वीक्रियते इत्य् उपादानम् । स काल उपादानं निमित्तं यस्मिन्, तम् आत्मानम् एव विश्व-रूपेणासृजत् । स्व-व्यतिरेकेण सृज्यस्याभावात् । एतच् च वस्तु-कथन-मात्रम् । कालेन निमित्तेन चासृजद् इत्य् एतावद् एव विवक्षितम् ॥११॥
word_for_word: with time as the instrumental cause
entries.literal_english: Here the general nature of time is stated, while a later chapter will explain it more specifically. Time is the disturbance of the guṇas, through which the transformation beginning with mahat is carried out. In itself time is without distinctions, but through its operation it produces the variations of creation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tatra sāmānyataḥ kālasya svarūpam atrocyate, uttarādhyāye tu viśeṣataḥ | guṇānāṃ vyatikaro mahad-ādi-pariṇāmas tenaivākriyate yaḥ, sa kāla iti śeṣaḥ | vakṣyate caikādaśe---guṇa-vyatikaraḥ kālaḥ svabhāvaḥ sūtram eva ca \[bhā|pu| 11.22.13\] iti | svatas tu nirviśeṣaḥ | apratiṣṭhitaḥ kvāpy aparyavasitaḥ, ādy-anta-śūnya ity arthaḥ | etad eva darśayitum īśvaraḥ sṛṣṭy-ādi tena nimitta-bhūtena karotīty āha---puruṣa iti | upādīyate nimittatayā svīkriyate ity upādānam | sa kāla upādānaṃ nimittaṃ yasmin, tam ātmānam eva viśva-rūpeṇāsṛjat | sva-vyatirekeṇa sṛjyasyābhāvāt | etac ca vastu-kathana-mātram | kālena nimittena cāsṛjad ity etāvad eva vivakṣitam ||11||

entries.sanskrit: स्व-व्यतिरिक्त-सृज्याभावं दर्शयन् कालस्य सृष्टि-निमित्ततां दर्शयति---विश्वम् इति । विष्णु-मायया संस्थितं संहृतं ब्रह्म-तन्-मात्रं सद् विश्वम् । ईश्वरेण कर्त्रा कालेन निमित्तेन परिच्छिन्नं पृथक् प्रकाशितम् । अव्यक्ता मूर्तिः स्वरूपं यस्येति स्वतो निर्विशेषता दर्शिता ॥१२॥
word_for_word: the absence of creation independent of Him
entries.literal_english: He shows that time is the cause of creation and that nothing created exists independently of the Lord. The world, held and withdrawn by Viṣṇu’s māyā, is made distinct and manifest by the Lord as agent, with time as the instrumental cause. The unmanifest form is the Lord’s own condition before differentiation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: sva-vyatirikta-sṛjyābhāvaṃ darśayan kālasya sṛṣṭi-nimittatāṃ darśayati---viśvam iti | viṣṇu-māyayā saṃsthitaṃ saṃhṛtaṃ brahma-tan-mātraṃ sad viśvam | īśvareṇa kartrā kālena nimittena paricchinnaṃ pṛthak prakāśitam | avyaktā mūrtiḥ svarūpaṃ yasyeti svato nirviśeṣatā darśitā ||12||

entries.sanskrit: अप्रतिष्ठितत्वं दर्शयितुं तत्-कार्य-विश्व-प्रवाहस्याप्रतिष्ठाम् आह---यथेदानीम् अस्ति तथाग्रे पूर्वम् अप्य् आसीत् पश्चाद् अपि भविष्यति ॥१३॥
word_for_word: the absence of a fixed beginning
entries.literal_english: To show that the stream of the world’s effects has no fixed beginning or end, he says: as it exists now, so it existed before and will exist afterward.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: apratiṣṭhitatvaṃ darśayituṃ tat-kārya-viśva-pravāhasyāpratiṣṭhām āha---yathedānīm asti tathāgre pūrvam apy āsīt paścād api bhaviṣyati ||13||

entries.sanskrit: एवं सामान्यतः कालं निरूप्य विशेषतो निरूपयिष्यंस् तन् निमित्तस्य सर्गस्य पूर्वोक्तान् एव भेदान् अनुवदति---सर्ग इति । यस् तु प्राकृतो वैकृतश् च स दशमः । तन् निमित्तम् एव त्रि-विधं प्रलयम् आह---कालेनैव केवलेन नित्यः प्रलयः । द्रव्येण सङ्कर्षणाग्न्य्-आदिना नैमित्तिकः । गुणैः स्व-स्व-कार्यं ग्रसद्भिः प्राकृतिकः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: he restates the divisions of creation
entries.literal_english: Having described time generally, he restates the previously mentioned divisions of the creation caused by it. The material and derivative creations together make ten. He then describes three kinds of dissolution: the constant dissolution produced by time alone, and the other dissolutions produced by the relevant causes.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: evaṃ sāmānyataḥ kālaṃ nirūpya viśeṣato nirūpayiṣyaṃs tan nimittasya sargasya pūrvoktān eva bhedān anuvadati---sarga iti | yas tu prākṛto vaikṛtaś ca sa daśamaḥ | tan nimittam eva tri-vidhaṃ pralayam āha---kālenaiva kevalena nityaḥ pralayaḥ | dravyeṇa saṅkarṣaṇāgny-ādinā naimittikaḥ | guṇaiḥ sva-sva-kāryaṃ grasadbhiḥ prākṛtikaḥ ||14||

entries.sanskrit: तान् एव सर्गान् प्रपञ्चयति---आद्य इत्य्-आदिना यावद्-अध्याय-समाप्ति । महतो लक्षणम् आत्मनो हरेः सकाशाद् गुणानां वैषम्यम् इति । अहमोऽहङ्कारस्य । तस्य लक्षणम्---यत्रेति । द्रव्यादयो वक्ष्यमाणास् त्रयः सर्गाः तन् मात्रो भूत-सर्गः, भूत-सूक्ष्म-सर्ग इत्य् अर्थः । द्रव्य-शक्तिमान् महा-भूतोत्पादकः ॥१५॥
entries.literal_english: He now expands the creations through the end of the chapter. Mahat is the inequality of the guṇas arising from Hari. Ahaṅkāra is explained by the place in which the transformations beginning with substance arise. The subsequent creations include the subtle elements, gross elements, senses, presiding deities and the other divisions of the created order.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tān eva sargān prapañcayati---ādya ity-ādinā yāvad-adhyāya-samāpti | mahato lakṣaṇam ātmano hareḥ sakāśād guṇānāṃ vaiṣamyam iti | ahamo’haṅkārasya | tasya lakṣaṇam---yatreti | dravyādayo vakṣyamāṇās trayaḥ sargāḥ tan mātro bhūta-sargaḥ, bhūta-sūkṣma-sarga ity arthaḥ | dravya-śaktimān mahā-bhūtotpādakaḥ ||15||

entries.sanskrit: ज्ञान-कर्मेन्द्रियात्मकश् चतुर्थः । पञ्चमो वैकारिकः इन्द्रियाधिष्ठातारो देवा मनश् च ॥१६॥
word_for_word: consisting of organs of knowledge and action
the deities presiding over the senses
entries.literal_english: The fourth creation is the group consisting of the organs of knowledge and action. The fifth is the vaikārika creation: the deities presiding over the senses together with the mind.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: jñāna-karmendriyātmakaś caturthaḥ | pañcamo vaikārikaḥ indriyādhiṣṭhātāro devā manaś ca ||16||

entries.sanskrit: षष्ठस् तु तमसः पञ्च-पर्वाविद्यायाः । अबुद्धिर् जीवानाम् आवरणं विक्षेपश् च तां करोतीत्य् अबुद्धि-कृत्तस्य । मे मत्तः शृणु ॥१७॥
entries.literal_english: The sixth creation is the fivefold ignorance arising from tamas. It produces the jīvas’ covering and distraction, called nonknowledge. Hear this explanation from Me.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: ṣaṣṭhas tu tamasaḥ pañca-parvāvidyāyāḥ | abuddhir jīvānām āvaraṇaṃ vikṣepaś ca tāṃ karotīty abuddhi-kṛttasya | me mattaḥ śṛṇu ||17||

entries.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगेन श्रोतव्यताम् आह---यद् विषया मेधा संसारं हरति, तस्य हरेर् लीला। यद् वा, इयम् इति तम-आदि-सर्ग-रूपा । रजो-भाज इति ब्रह्म-रूपस्येत्य् अर्थः । अस्मिन् पक्षे अबुद्धि-कृत इति प्रथमान्तम् । अनवधान-कृत इत्य् अर्थः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: that it should be heard without agitation
in the form of creation beginning with darkness
of those who partake of rajas
entries.literal_english: He says that it should be heard without agitation. It is the Lord’s līlā that removes the mind’s attraction to sense objects and saṃsāra; alternatively, “this” refers to the creation beginning with darkness. “Those who partake of rajas” refers to Brahmā’s rajasic form; “created by nonknowledge” can also be read as caused by inattention.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: anudvegena śrotavyatām āha---yad viṣayā medhā saṃsāraṃ harati, tasya harer līlā| yad vā, iyam iti tama-ādi-sarga-rūpā | rajo-bhāja iti brahma-rūpasyety arthaḥ | asmin pakṣe abuddhi-kṛta iti prathamāntam | anavadhāna-kṛta ity arthaḥ ||18||

entries.sanskrit: मुख्यम् इव प्रथमं कृतो मुख्य-सर्गः । तस्थुषां स्थावराणाम् । षड्-विधत्वम् एवाह---ये पूष्पं विना फलन्ति ते वनस्पतयः । ओषधयः फल-पाकान्ताः । लता आरोहणापेक्षाः । त्वक्-सारा वेण्व्-आदयः । लता एव काठिन्येन आरोहणानपेक्षा वीरुधः । ये पुष्पैः फलन्ति ते द्रुमाः ॥१९॥
word_for_word: made first, as it were, primary
entries.literal_english: The primary creation is called primary because it was made first. The stationary beings are sixfold: trees that bear fruit without flowers, herbs that end in fruit, creepers that require support, plants whose essence is bark such as bamboo, creepers that are hard and do not require climbing support, and trees that bear fruit through flowers.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: mukhyam iva prathamaṃ kṛto mukhya-sargaḥ | tasthuṣāṃ sthāvarāṇām | ṣaḍ-vidhatvam evāha---ye pūṣpaṃ vinā phalanti te vanaspatayaḥ | oṣadhayaḥ phala-pākāntāḥ | latā ārohaṇāpekṣāḥ | tvak-sārā veṇv-ādayaḥ | latā eva kāṭhinyena ārohaṇānapekṣā vīrudhaḥ | ye puṣpaiḥ phalanti te drumāḥ ||19||

entries.sanskrit: तेषां साधारणं लक्षणम् आह---ऊर्ध्वं स्रोतः आहार-सञ्चारो येषाम् । तमः-प्राया अव्यक्त-चैतन्याः । अन्तः-स्पर्शाः स्पर्शम् एव जानन्ति नान्यत् । तद् अप्य् अन्तर् एव न बहिः। विशेषिणोऽव्यवस्थित-परिणामाद्य्-अनेक-भेदवन्तः ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: Their common characteristics are now given. Their nourishment flows upward; they are predominantly tamasic and their consciousness is unmanifest. They know only internal touch, not external objects; even that touch is inward. Their distinguishing forms include many kinds of unstable transformation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: teṣāṃ sādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇam āha---ūrdhvaṃ srotaḥ āhāra-sañcāro yeṣām | tamaḥ-prāyā avyakta-caitanyāḥ | antaḥ-sparśāḥ sparśam eva jānanti nānyat | tad apy antar eva na bahiḥ| viśeṣiṇo’vyavasthita-pariṇāmādy-aneka-bhedavantaḥ ||20||

entries.sanskrit: तिर्यक् स्रोतसां सर्गम् आह---तिरश्चाम् इति । स च अष्टाविंशति-भेदः । तिरश्चां लक्षणम् । अविदः श्वस्तनादि-ज्ञान-शून्याः । भूरि-तमसः आहारादि-ज्ञान-मात्र-निष्ठाः । घ्राणेनैवेष्टम् अर्थं जानन्ति । हृदि अवेदिनो दीर्घानुसन्धान् अशून्याः । तथा च श्रुतिः---अथेतरेषां पशूनाम् अशनापिपासे एवाभिविज्ञानं न विज्ञातं वदन्ति, न विज्ञातं पश्यन्ति, न विदुः श्वस्तनं न लोकालोकौ इति ॥२१॥
word_for_word: the creation whose current moves sideways
they know the desired object through smell
entries.literal_english: He describes the creation whose current moves sideways: the animals. It has twenty-eight divisions. They lack knowledge of tomorrow and the like, are heavily covered by darkness, know mainly food and related objects, recognize what they need through smell, and have no extended inward reflection.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tiryak srotasāṃ sargam āha---tiraścām iti | sa ca aṣṭāviṃśati-bhedaḥ | tiraścāṃ lakṣaṇam | avidaḥ śvastanādi-jñāna-śūnyāḥ | bhūri-tamasaḥ āhārādi-jñāna-mātra-niṣṭhāḥ | ghrāṇenaiveṣṭam arthaṃ jānanti | hṛdi avedino dīrghānusandhān aśūnyāḥ | tathā ca śrutiḥ---athetareṣāṃ paśūnām aśanāpipāse evābhivijñānaṃ na vijñātaṃ vadanti, na vijñātaṃ paśyanti, na viduḥ śvastanaṃ na lokālokau iti ||21||

entries.sanskrit: अष्टा-विंशति-भेदान् एवाह---गवादय उष्ट्रान्ता द्वि-शफा द्वि-खुरा नव ॥२१॥ स्वरादय एक-शफाः षत् । अष्टा-विंशति-भेदान् एवाह---गवादय उष्ट्रान्ता द्वि-शफा द्वि-खुरा नव ।श्वादयो गोधान्ताः पञ्च-नखा द्वादश । एवम् एते भू-चराः सप्त-विंशतिः । मकरादयो जल-चराः। कङ्कादयश् च स्व-गा अभूचरत्वेनैकी-कृत्य गृहीताः । तद् एवम् अष्टा-विंशति-भेदा भवन्ति । तेषु कृष्ण-रुरु-गौरा मृग-विशेषाः । अन्येषाम् अपि तिर्यक् प्राणिनां यथा-यथम् एतेष्व् एवान्तर् भावः ॥२२-२५॥
word_for_word: aquatic creatures beginning with the makara
entries.literal_english: He lists the twenty-eight animal divisions: the two-hoofed animals beginning with the cow and ending with the camel, the single-hoofed animals beginning with the horse, and the five-nailed animals beginning with the dog and ending with the alligator. These make the terrestrial classes; aquatic creatures such as the makara make the water-dwelling classes, and birds and the other divisions complete the twenty-eight forms. The commentary explains the bodily signs and the characteristic knowledge of each class.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: aṣṭā-viṃśati-bhedān evāha---gavādaya uṣṭrāntā dvi-śaphā dvi-khurā nava ||21|| svarādaya eka-śaphāḥ ṣat | aṣṭā-viṃśati-bhedān evāha---gavādaya uṣṭrāntā dvi-śaphā dvi-khurā nava |śvādayo godhāntāḥ pañca-nakhā dvādaśa | evam ete bhū-carāḥ sapta-viṃśatiḥ | makarādayo jala-carāḥ| kaṅkādayaś ca sva-gā abhūcaratvenaikī-kṛtya gṛhītāḥ | tad evam aṣṭā-viṃśati-bhedā bhavanti | teṣu kṛṣṇa-ruru-gaurā mṛga-viśeṣāḥ | anyeṣām api tiryak prāṇināṃ yathā-yatham eteṣv evāntar bhāvaḥ ||22-25||

entries.sanskrit: अध आहार-सञ्चारो यस्य सोऽर्वाक्-स्रोतः । ह्रस्वत्वम् आर्षम् । नृणां सर्गो नृणां लक्षणम् । रजोऽधिकं येषु ते ॥२६॥
entries.literal_english: The downward-moving current is the human creation. The expression is shortened in the ancient usage. The creation of human beings is defined by human characteristics, and those in whom rajas predominates belong to this class.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: adha āhāra-sañcāro yasya so’rvāk-srotaḥ | hrasvatvam ārṣam | nṛṇāṃ sargo nṛṇāṃ lakṣaṇam | rajo’dhikaṃ yeṣu te ||26||

entries.sanskrit: एते त्रयो वैकृता एव न कौमारवद् उभयात्मकाः । देव-स्र्गश् च वैकृत इत्य् अनुषङ्गः । वैकारिकस् तु देव-सर्गः प्राकृतेषु पूर्वम् एव प्रोक्तः । अयं तु ततो न्यूनत्वाद् वैकृतो देव-सर्गत्वात् तद् अन्तर्-भूतश् च । सनत्-कुमारादीनां सर्गस् तु प्राकृतो वैकृतश् च देवत्वेन मनुष्यत्वेन च सृज्य इत्य् अर्थः ॥२७॥
word_for_word: not mixed material-and-derivative as the Kumāra creation
the creation of Sanat-kumāra and the others
entries.literal_english: These three are derivative creations, not mixed material-and-derivative creations like the Kumāra creation. The divine creation is also derivative. The vaikārika divine creation had already been mentioned among the material creations; this later divine creation is derivative because it is a subsequent and lesser manifestation. The creation of Sanat-kumāra and the others is both material and derivative.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: ete trayo vaikṛtā eva na kaumāravad ubhayātmakāḥ | deva-srgaś ca vaikṛta ity anuṣaṅgaḥ | vaikārikas tu deva-sargaḥ prākṛteṣu pūrvam eva proktaḥ | ayaṃ tu tato nyūnatvād vaikṛto deva-sargatvāt tad antar-bhūtaś ca | sanat-kumārādīnāṃ sargas tu prākṛto vaikṛtaś ca devatvena manuṣyatvena ca sṛjya ity arthaḥ ||27||

entries.sanskrit: वैकृतश् च देव-सर्गोऽष्ट-विधः । तत्र विबुधादयस् त्रयो भेदाः । गन्धर्वाप्सरस एकः । यक्ष-रक्षांस्य् एकः । भूत-प्रेत-पिशाचा एकः । सिद्ध-चारण-विद्याधरा एकः । किन्नरादय एकः । आदि-शब्दात् किंपुरुषाश्व-मुखादयः । एतद् विंशेऽध्याये स्पष्टं भविष्यति ॥२८-२९॥
word_for_word: the derivative divine creation is eightfold
entries.literal_english: The derivative divine creation is eightfold: the gods and related beings, the Gandharvas and Apsarases, the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, the ghosts and Piśācas, the Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Vidyādharas, and the Kinnaras and related beings. The “etc.” includes Kimpuruṣas and horse-faced beings; the detailed account appears later.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: vaikṛtaś ca deva-sargo’ṣṭa-vidhaḥ | tatra vibudhādayas trayo bhedāḥ | gandharvāpsarasa ekaḥ | yakṣa-rakṣāṃsy ekaḥ | bhūta-preta-piśācā ekaḥ | siddha-cāraṇa-vidyādharā ekaḥ | kinnarādaya ekaḥ | ādi-śabdāt kiṃpuruṣāśva-mukhādayaḥ | etad viṃśe’dhyāye spaṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati ||28-29||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; Śrīdhara marks 3.10.30 as not explained.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तर्हि प्रथमं सृष्टिः प्रलयो वा, तत्राह---गुणेति । गुण-व्यत्यये सर्गे भ्राम्यन् भ्रमण-शीलो भ्रमिर् अविशेषाद् भ्राम्यद् भ्रमिस् तस्य नद्यां भ्रमतो यथा नादिर् नान्तस् तथा सृष्टि-संहारयोर् इत्य् अर्थः । संसारस्यानादित्वम् एक-रूपत्वं चाह---देवासुरादय इति । त एवेति । तन्-नामानस् तद्-रूपाश् चेत्य् अर्थः ॥३१-३२॥
word_for_word: in creation through disturbance of the guṇas
entries.literal_english: Creation and dissolution do not have a first point. In the disturbance of the guṇas the wandering world moves like a whirlpool; just as a person circling in a river cannot find its beginning or end, so no beginning or end of creation and dissolution is found. Saṃsāra is beginningless and its pattern remains continuous through gods, demons and the other beings.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: nanu tarhi prathamaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ pralayo vā, tatrāha---guṇeti | guṇa-vyatyaye sarge bhrāmyan bhramaṇa-śīlo bhramir aviśeṣād bhrāmyad bhramis tasya nadyāṃ bhramato yathā nādir nāntas tathā sṛṣṭi-saṃhārayor ity arthaḥ | saṃsārasyānāditvam eka-rūpatvaṃ cāha---devāsurādaya iti | ta eveti | tan-nāmānas tad-rūpāś cety arthaḥ ||31-32||
